drive._shaper_note: decel-into-the-goal campaign (2026-07-22): a_max/a_decel/j_max/yaw_jerk_max read again by gen_boot_config.py's shaper_config_for_config() (Motion::VelocityShaper) -- see tovez.json's own _shaper_note for the full history/derivation. alpha_max/alpha_decel are new this campaign; 7.0rad/s^2 matches tovez.json's own value/derivation, touched only to stay schema-complete (togov mecanum bench characterization remains out of scope, same posture as this file's own _sprint_114_note above). j_max/yaw_jerk_max power the jerk-limited S-curve stage (same day) -- values unchanged.
drive._drive_calibration_note: duty_per_speed_* [duty/(mm/s)]: open-loop wheel calibration, the inverse of the measured plant gain (speed_sweep 2026-07-27: L ~560, R ~510 mm/s per duty; ceiling ~500 mm/s). Per-wheel because the two gearboxes differ ~10%. crawl_pulse [-1,1]: fixed pulse amplitude for sub-breakaway wheel speeds, Bresenham-dithered in App::Drive; 0 disables. Measured breakaway is 1-6% duty and state-dependent (src/tests/firmware/duty_min/RESULTS.md) -- the earlier 0.20 was sized against a duty_sweep criterion that the standalone prober disproved, so crawl ships OFF pending a re-measure of the low end.
drive._wheel_correction_note: IDENTITY as of 2026-07-31 (stakeholder). The fitted values (tovez: gain ~1.47) were measured against a duty_per_speed that was itself wrong by ~1.6x, so the pair was circularly calibrated -- each fitted against the other's error -- and the correction ended up pointing the WRONG WAY: it divided a 150mm/s request down to 96 before the duty conversion, on a robot that was already under-delivering. duty_per_speed is now a baked measured constant (App::Drive::kDutyPerSpeed), so this affine stage has nothing left to correct and is held at identity. Do not re-fit it against duty_per_speed again; refit only against camera-measured travel, and say so here. gain 1 / intercept 0 = no correction.

Held at 0.0, the documented INERT state -- matching this file's own existing wheel_control posture (see _wheel_controller_note below: togov has no drive characterization of its own, so every Stage B/C key ships 0/disabled rather than borrowing tovez's numbers for an uncharacterized drivetrain), the same posture gopiv.json's 2026-08-09 precedent established for a different uncharacterized robot. Do not borrow tovez's measured 15.0/40.0/500.0 -- that would be a fabricated calibration, not a default.
wheel_control._pos_err_max_note: 133-002: Stage B's position-error clamp [mm] -- the INPUT-side bound on the I term, distinct from pid_i_max's OUTPUT-side [mm/s] bound; both retained. 0 = unclamped, matching every other wheel_control key on this robot: togov has no drive characterization of its own, so both Stage B and Stage C stay disabled rather than borrowing tovez's numbers (see the note below).
wheel_control._wheel_controller_note: 130-004 (wheel-speed-controller-moves-into-drive.md): App::Drive's unified three-timescale controller. togov (mecanum, 4 wheels) has NO population duty-sweep characterization of its own -- ticket 001's sweep ran on tovez's differential drive pair only. All wheel_*/deficit_* keys held at 0 (both Stage B fast-PID AND Stage C bias-trim adaptation disabled, matching this file's own control.wheel_gain_*/_wheel_correction_note precedent of shipping IDENTITY/inert values rather than borrowing tovez's numbers for an uncharacterized drivetrain) -- unlike the planner._uncalibrated borrow-with-flag pattern elsewhere in this file, 0 here is a SAFE, meaningful disabled state (Stage A's existing conversion map keeps working unmodified), not a placeholder standing in for a value the code requires nonzero to function. Replace with togov's own duty-sweep results before enabling either stage.
